questions.question: If $\begin{vmatrix} x & 2 \\ 18 & x \end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix} 6 & 2 \\ 18 & 6 \end{vmatrix}$, then $x$ is equal to:

solution.concept: $\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix} = ad - bc$
solution.mistake: Writing only $x = 6$; a square equation gives two roots, $\pm 6$.

questions.question: If $A$ is a square matrix of order 3 with $|A| = 5$, then $|\text{adj}\, A|$ is:

solution.concept: For a square matrix of order $n$, $|\text{adj}\, A| = |A|^{n-1}$.

steps.do: Use the property of the adjoint.

solution.mistake: Using $|A|^n = 125$; the power is $n - 1$, not $n$.

questions.question: If $A$ is a square matrix of order 3 and $|A| = 4$, then $|2A|$ is:

solution.concept: For a square matrix of order $n$, $|kA| = k^n |A|$.

steps.do: Use the property for a scalar multiple.

solution.mistake: Writing $|2A| = 2|A| = 8$; each of the 3 rows is multiplied by 2.

questions.question: The area of the triangle with vertices $(-2, -3)$, $(3, 2)$ and $(-1, -8)$ is:

solution.concept: Area $\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$, taken with absolute value.

steps.do: Write the area as a determinant.
Area is always positive, so take the absolute value.

solution.mistake: Forgetting the $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and choosing $30$ sq units.

questions.question: The cofactor of the element $a_{12}$ in $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -3 & 5 \\ 6 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 5 & -7 \end{vmatrix}$ is:

solution.concept: Cofactor $A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} M_{ij}$, where $M_{ij}$ is the minor.

steps.do: Delete row 1 and column 2 to get the minor $M_{12}$.

solution.mistake: Giving the minor $-46$ as the answer and forgetting the sign $(-1)^{i+j}$.

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** If $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix with $|A| = 2$, then $|A\,(\text{adj}\, A)| = 8$. **Reason (R):** For any square matrix $A$, $A\,(\text{adj}\, A) = |A|\, I$.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

solution.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.concept: $A(\text{adj}\, A) = (\text{adj}\, A)A = |A|\, I$ for every square matrix $A$.

steps.do: Check A: use $A(\text{adj}\, A) = |A| I$ with $n = 3$.
Check R: $A(\text{adj}\, A) = |A| I$ is a standard theorem, so R is true.
A is obtained directly from R, so R correctly explains A.

solution.mistake: Taking $\big||A| I\big| = |A| = 2$; a scalar comes out of a $3 \times 3$ determinant as $|A|^3$.

questions.question: Find the values of $k$ if the area of the triangle with vertices $(k, 0)$, $(4, 0)$ and $(0, 2)$ is $4$ sq units.

solution.concept: Area $= \pm \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$, so use both signs.

steps.do: Write the area as a determinant.
Area is $4$, so the determinant value can be $+4$ or $-4$.

solution.mistake: Taking only $4 - k = 4$ and missing the second value $k = 8$.

questions.question: Find the adjoint and inverse of $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$.

solution.concept: $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\, \text{adj}\, A$, provided $|A| \neq 0$.

steps.do: For a $2 \times 2$ matrix, swap the diagonal and change signs of the others.
steps.math: \text{adj}\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}

solution.mistake: Changing the signs of the diagonal elements instead of the off-diagonal ones.

questions.question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$, show that $A^2 - 5A + 7I = O$. Hence find $A^{-1}$.

solution.concept: Multiply the matrix equation by $A^{-1}$ and use $A^{-1}A = I$.
solution.mistake: Writing $5 - A$ instead of $5I - A$; a number cannot be subtracted from a matrix.

questions.question: Using determinants, find the equation of the line joining the points $(1, 2)$ and $(3, 6)$.

solution.concept: Three points are collinear when the area determinant is zero.

steps.do: Let $P(x, y)$ be any point on the line.
$P$, $(1, 2)$, $(3, 6)$ are collinear, so the area is zero.
Simplify to get the required line.

solution.mistake: Expanding the determinant with wrong signs; the middle term of $R_1$ is $-y(\ldots)$.

questions.question: Solve the system of equations using the matrix method: $5x + 2y = 4$, $7x + 3y = 5$.

solution.concept: If $AX = B$ and $|A| \neq 0$, then $X = A^{-1}B$ (unique solution).

steps.why: So the system has a unique solution.

solution.mistake: Writing $X = BA^{-1}$; the order must be $A^{-1}B$.

questions.question: Examine the consistency of the system: $x + 3y = 5$, $2x + 6y = 8$.

solution.answer: Inconsistent (no solution), since $|A| = 0$ and $(\text{adj}\, A)B \neq O$
solution.concept: If $|A| = 0$ and $(\text{adj}\, A)B \neq O$, the system is inconsistent.

steps.do: Hence the system is inconsistent (it has no solution).

solution.mistake: Stopping at $|A| = 0$; you must also check $(\text{adj}\, A)B$ before concluding.

questions.question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$, show that $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{19}A$.

steps.do: Take the minus sign inside the matrix.

solution.mistake: Losing the negative sign of $|A| = -19$ when writing $A^{-1}$.

questions.question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & -4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$, verify that $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

solution.concept: Reversal law: $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

steps.do: Both sides are equal, so $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$ is verified.

solution.mistake: Multiplying $A^{-1}B^{-1}$ instead of $B^{-1}A^{-1}$; matrix order matters.

questions.question: A school wants to allocate students into three clubs: Sports, Music and Drama, under the following conditions: (i) the number of students in the Sports club should be equal to the sum of the numbers of students in the Music and Drama clubs; (ii) the number of students in the Music club should be 20 more than half the number of students in the Sports club; (iii) the total number of students allocated to the three clubs is 180. Using the matrix method, find the number of students allocated to each club.

solution.concept: Form $AX = B$; if $|A| \neq 0$, then $X = A^{-1}B$ with $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\,\text{adj}\, A$.

steps.do: Let the numbers in Sports, Music and Drama be $x$, $y$, $z$.
Write the three conditions as equations.
steps.math: x - y - z = 0, \qquad -x + 2y = 40, \qquad x + y + z = 180

steps.why: So $A^{-1}$ exists and the solution is unique.

steps.do: Find the cofactors of rows 2 and 3.

solution.mistake: Writing condition (ii) as $y = \tfrac{1}{2}(x + 20)$; it is $y = \tfrac{x}{2} + 20$.

questions.question: Find the product $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0 & 1 \\ 9 & 2 & -3 \\ 6 & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$ and use it to solve: $x - y + 2z = 1$, $2y - 3z = 1$, $3x - 2y + 4z = 2$.

solution.concept: If $AB = I$, then $A^{-1} = B$.

steps.do: Call the first matrix $A$ and the second $B$. Multiply row by column.
Since $AB = I$, $B$ is the inverse of $A$.
Write the system as $AX = C$; its coefficient matrix is $A$.

solution.mistake: Forgetting the $0$ coefficient of $x$ in $2y - 3z = 1$ when writing row 2 of $A$.

questions.question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & -3 & -4 \end{bmatrix}$, find $A^{-1}$. Hence solve: $x + 2y - 3z = -4$, $2x + 3y + 2z = 2$, $3x - 3y - 4z = 11$.

steps.do: The system is $AX = B$ with this $A$, so $X = A^{-1}B$.

solution.mistake: Using the cofactor matrix itself as $\text{adj}\, A$; it must be transposed.

questions.question: The cost of 4 kg onion, 3 kg wheat and 2 kg rice is ₹60. The cost of 2 kg onion, 4 kg wheat and 6 kg rice is ₹90. The cost of 6 kg onion, 2 kg wheat and 3 kg rice is ₹70. Find the cost of each item per kg by the matrix method.

solution.answer: Onion ₹5 per kg, wheat ₹8 per kg, rice ₹8 per kg
solution.concept: Form $AX = B$; if $|A| \neq 0$, then $X = A^{-1}B$.

steps.do: Let onion, wheat and rice cost ₹$x$, ₹$y$, ₹$z$ per kg.
Find the cofactors of rows 2 and 3.
Hence onion costs ₹5 per kg, wheat ₹8 per kg and rice ₹8 per kg.

solution.mistake: Mixing up the order of items in a row; keep onion, wheat, rice in the same order.

solution.concept: The coefficient matrix here is $A'$, and $(A')^{-1} = (A^{-1})'$.

steps.do: Write the system in matrix form $CX = B$.
The rows of $C$ are the columns of $A$, so $C = A'$.
steps.why: Inverse of a transpose is the transpose of the inverse.

solution.mistake: Using $X = A^{-1}B$ directly; the coefficient matrix is $A'$, not $A$.

questions.question: **Case Study:** A farmer owns a triangular plot of land whose corners, on a map grid, are $A(2, 3)$, $B(-1, 0)$ and $C(3, -2)$ (1 unit = 10 m). He plans to fix a pole at a point $D(k, 1)$ on the boundary line $AB$.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Using determinants, find the area of the plot in square units.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Find the value of $k$ so that $D$ lies on line $AB$.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Using determinants, find the equation of line $AB$.

solution.concept: Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\right|$; collinear points give area zero.

steps.do: Write the area as a determinant.
Hence area of the plot $= 9$ sq units.
steps.why: On the ground this is $9 \times 100 = 900$ m².

steps.do: $D$ on line $AB$ means $A$, $B$, $D$ are collinear, so area is zero.
Hence $k = 0$, so the pole is at $D(0, 1)$.
Let $P(x, y)$ be any point on $AB$; $P$, $A$, $B$ are collinear.
Divide by 3 to get the equation of line $AB$.

solution.mistake: In (ii), using $C$ instead of $B$; $D$ must be collinear with $A$ and $B$.
